newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NEW HUNGARY POLLS PUT GOVERNING SOCIALISTS AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: NEW HUNGARY POLLS PUT GOVERNING SOCIALISTS AHEAD.

text.p: Hungary's senior governing party, the Socialists, have restored their position as the country's most popular party, according to two polls published at the weekend.
A Gallup poll gave the Socialist Party (MSZP) 30 percent while the opposition parties the Federation of Young Democrats (Fidesz) and the Independent Smallholders (FKGP) scored 27 and 21 percent each.
A Szonda-Ipsos poll released earlier put the MSZP even further ahead with 31 percent, compared to 22 percent for Fidesz and 21 percent for the Smallholders.

Previous polls had put the two opposition parties level or slightly ahead of the Socialists, led by Prime Minister Gyula Horn, and prompted concerns within the Horn's party ahead of a congress earlier this month that it may lose elections due in May next year.

Analysts put the rise in popularity down to a general good news factor -- including positive signs in the economy and an expected invitation for Hungary to join NATO later this month -- and a well-organised show of unity at the congress held on June 9.

"The (Socialists) have effectively begun campaigning," political analyst Attila Ledenyi told Reuters. "The public has been getting a lot of positive messages over the past month or so and the added publicity of a disciplined party congress also helped boost their image."
The Socialists' junior coalition partner, the Alliance of Free Democrats, also improved its rating, to nine percent, compared to scores of seven to eight in surveys earlier this year.
The two parties together gained around 53 percent of the popular vote in the 1994 election, giving them a 72 percent majority of seats in Parliament.
